pinterest.title: Mykonos Wedding Season: Weather by Month from the Nearest Official Station
pinterest.description: Our guide reads the Mykonos season from Naxos, the nearest official weather station. There, June to August are the driest months, with under one rain day a month in July and August, May and September sit milder, and October brings 38.6 mm of rain over 5.5 days. The prevailing wind blows from the north in every month, so plan the ceremony time around summer heat and the wind, and keep a covered fallback in place.

pinterest.title: Mykonos Wedding Venues: Private Chapels, Beach Settings and Sunset Terraces
pinterest.description: Settle the kind of place before the name. Kivotos and Ftelia Bay Hotel each have a private chapel, Mykonos Blu holds ceremonies on The Ocean Balcony above Psarou beach, Royal Myconian lists a private spot on Elia Beach, and Saint John Hotel Villas & Spa sits on the sunset coast at Agios Ioannis. Our guide sets out what each setting suits and the questions to ask before you sign.

pinterest.title: Planning a Mykonos Wedding: House Rules to Agree Before You Book
pinterest.description: A venue's rules shape the day as much as its view. Before you sign, ask about music times, exclusive use, deposits, cancellation, ceremony times, the weather plan for a strong north wind or a heatwave, suppliers, packages and guest rooms. Then get every answer in the contract or a written confirmation, not a chat thread. Our Mykonos wedding guide lists the questions to send each venue.

slides: Mykonos is on your shortlist. Before you ask a single venue for a quote, settle the area, the season and the kind of place.
Think in evenings, not maps: Hora and Little Venice keep guests close to town, the beaches put sand below the ceremony, and Agios Ioannis faces the sunset.
Pick the setting before the name: a hotel with a private chapel, a beachfront resort, a large resort with several spaces, or a private villa.
Five venues to start a shortlist: Mykonos Blu, Kivotos, Saint John Hotel Villas & Spa, Ftelia Bay Hotel and Royal Myconian. Examples, not a ranking.
Season: at Naxos, the nearest official weather station, June to August are the driest months, with May and September milder.
Mind the wind as much as the heat. The north wind blows in every month at Naxos, so ask each venue where the ceremony sits and what shelter it has.
Get the house rules in writing before you sign: music times, exclusive use, deposits, cancellation, ceremony times and the weather plan.
Planning your own Mykonos wedding? Send us your month, guest count and the venues you have in mind, and a Wedded Advisor will talk it through with you. Link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Planning a Mykonos wedding?

Mykonos sits in the heart of the Cyclades and is known as the island of the winds. Paved lanes, white houses, small chapels and the windmills above Hora are the picture couples carry with them, and in Little Venice the houses are built right against the sea.

Our new guide takes the big decisions in order. It starts with the area and the kind of venue that suit your guest list: hotels with a private chapel, beachfront resorts, large resorts with several spaces, and private villas. Five venues get you started: Mykonos Blu on Psarou, Kivotos, Saint John Hotel Villas & Spa in Agios Ioannis, Ftelia Bay Hotel on Ftelia Beach and Royal Myconian on Elia Beach.

It then reads the season from Naxos, the nearest official weather station, with weather by month and how to plan the ceremony time around summer heat and the north wind.

It closes with the house rules to agree in writing before you book, and what shapes the overall cost.

Planning your own Mykonos wedding? Send us a message with your month, guest count and the venues you are weighing up. Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish. Full guide at the link in our bio.
